subject: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline

Team —

Horizon AI (attached intro + requirements) wants to run a 6-week APAC pilot starting Oct 6. They signed a preliminary commercial LOI (deal id DEAL-2026-1487-HZN) and the ask is: dedicated APAC pool with EU/US failover lanes for resilience. High level numbers from their traffic profile:

- Peak concurrent inference sessions: ~2,200 (mostly chat/assistant use)
- 95th percentile token throughput: ~11,000 tokens/sec across the fleet
- Preferred model family: openspan/13B quantized -> we should plan for 40 q8 BL instances equivalent (estimate below)
- SLOs: p95 latency < 300ms for interactive flows; retry budget 0.5%

Initial sizing suggestion (very rough):
- APAC dedicated pool: 10 nodes (A100-80GB equiv) with continuous batching and prefix caching configured; this gives baseline throughput for the pilot with headroom for peak spikes.
- EU/US failover: 4 nodes each in respective regions, configured for warm standby with KV cache sync window.

We need operational answers by EOD Fri (9/17) on:
1) Feasibility of provisioning APAC nodes by Oct 6 (including network/VPC prep).
2) Confirmation of the 10/4/4 split or suggested alternatives (I used a conservative approach).
3) Any known capacity or supply constraints (spot shortages, procurement lead times) that would force a delayed start.

I've attached the pilot_capacity_sheet.xlsx with the basic traffic to cost mapping and a suggested rollout cadence. Horizon is flexible on instance shapes if we can show cost parity + latency.

Next steps I'm planning: internal alignment first, then share SOW draft + procurement checklist with Horizon so they can fast-track approvals.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: pilot_capacity_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline

Laura — thanks for the clear ask and the sheet. Quick notes from the capacity/infra side: 

- Provisioning time: if we use our existing Singapore region capacity pool, we can provision 10 nodes under Dedicated in ~6 business days for a pilot (assuming no additional cloud limit increases). If new physical racks are required, that moves to 4-6 weeks, but I don't expect that for this pilot.
- Node shape: A100-80GB equiv is fine; q8 quantized 13B models are very CPU/GPU kernel friendly but KV cache pressure matters. I'll size with a ratio that assumes 30% of persistent RAM used by cached prefixes.
- EU/US warm standby: warm standby with 4 nodes each is doable, but note that cache-warmup costs (network egress + initial burst) can spike costs. Suggesting an alternate: 6 APAC + 3 EU + 3 US for lower total headroom but quicker global failover tests (less warm capacity overall).

Risks/blocks:
- We currently have two enterprise commitments that overlap Oct 1-15 in APAC which may reduce available burst buffer; if Horizon needs strict SLA with no degraded mode, we should move to 12 APAC nodes or secure burst credit.
- Networking/VPC peering and KMS provisioning usually take 1-2 business days once procurement provides required CIDR/KMS IDs.

Action items I need from Laura by EOD Thu: confirmed target start date, and whether Horizon can accept limited degraded capacity for first 2 weeks (we can heavily instrument and offer credits if not met). I can run a quick cost delta for the 10/4/4 vs 6/3/3 split once you confirm.
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline

Laura & team — attaching a quick SOW draft (SOW-draft-Horizon-20260915.pdf). Key commercial contingencies for procurement:

- Pilot term: 6 weeks, fixed price covering dedicated APAC pool + failover lanes, with a usage overlay for token overage beyond the agreed forecast.
- Upfront commitment: 50% of pilot cost due on activation to reserve Dedicated nodes.
- SLA: we will provide a 99.5% availability target for the dedicated pool during pilot; penalties / credits to be negotiated if degraded beyond agreed thresholds.
- Data handling: Horizon requires SOC2 evidence and ability to restrict any logs to their VPC; we will provide audit-read access and redaction controls.

Procurement path: I can send this SOW + standard redwood MSA to procurement@horizon.ai once Laura confirms the start date and the capacity split. Please note: finance needs at least 3 business days to process the pilot invoice once we have PO number.

Attachment: SOW-draft-Horizon-20260915.pdf (pdf, 7 pages)

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

From: Sam Park <sam@horizon.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizon.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:12:00 +0800
Subject: Re: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline

Hi Laura / Steph — thanks for the detail. Quick confirmations from Horizon: 

- We can start pilot onboarding the week of Oct 6; procurement will issue a PO within 3 business days of SOW receipt.
- Horizon is okay with the 6/3/3 alternative Karthik suggested (we prefer lower committed cost). We do want a documented failover plan that guarantees cold start < 60s and progressive KV priming during low-traffic hours.
- Security: SOC2 Type II report is required; we'll also need the KMS thumbprint and details on retention of traces.

Two asks from our side before we sign SOW:
1) A brief runbook for failover behavior (5-8 bullets) describing how traffic is rerouted and expected warmup costs.
2) A short test plan for week 2 of the pilot to exercise EU and US failover lanes (we want to validate cross-region latency during simulated outages).

We'll review the SOW and get PO over as soon as the runbook is included.

Cheers,
Sam Park
Head of Platform Partnerships, Horizon AI
sam@horizon.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam@horizon.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: APAC pilot + tri-region failover: capacity sizing and timeline

Thanks all — summarized next steps and owners below. Agreeing to the 6 APAC / 3 EU / 3 US split per Horizon preference while we keep an eye on October burst windows.

Owners & timeline: 
- Karthik: finalize provisioning plan + estimate of warmup cost delta for 6/3/3 vs 10/4/4 by Mon 9/20 COB. (Karthik)
- Stephanie: attach runbook section into SOW and reissue to procurement@horizon.ai with PO instructions by Fri 9/17 EOD (Steph).
- Finance: prepare pilot invoice template and payment instructions (Finance note: need PO before activation).
- Laura: schedule kickoff call with Horizon for Oct 5 (pre-deployment checklist) and confirm internal monitoring dashboards + alert thresholds.

Horizon — please confirm PO cadence for us to time activation. If procurement can get the PO within 48 hours of SOW receipt we can lock the Oct 6 start. Otherwise we may need to shift to Oct 13 to accommodate finance processing and soft provisioning windows.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Oct 5 kickoff once Steph uploads the SOW with runbook.

Best,
Laura
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
